title: personal-llm-experiment-tracker-ryan-2026
content:
Personal LLM inference experiment tracker - quick mini-sheet

Purpose: lightweight scratchpad to track small experiments tuning runtime/config (batching, quantization, kv cache) and simple evals. Keep it terse.

Notes to self:
- focus on realistic prompt mix (median seq ~ 256, p95 ~ 1024)
- prioritize configs that reduce cost without exceeding 200ms tail latency for interactive routes
- run 3 seeds for perf numbers where noise >5%

EXPERIMENT TABLE (columns: id | date | model | quant | batch | kv_cache | sequence | throughput (tokens/s) | p50 latency(ms) | p95 latency(ms) | cost_per_1k_tokens | eval_metric (QA F1 / slot accuracy) | notes)

E1 | 2026-02-10 | gpt-medium-open | int8 | dynamic batching 32 | enabled | 256 | 8,400 | 45 | 210 | $0.82 | QA F1 0.78 | baseline for medium model; stable; perf good but cost high
E2 | 2026-02-11 | gpt-medium-open | int8 | dynamic batching 16 | enabled | 256 | 6,100 | 38 | 170 | $0.95 | QA F1 0.77 | lower batch reduces throughput but improves p95
E3 | 2026-02-12 | gpt-medium-open | 4-bit | dynamic batching 32 | enabled | 256 | 7,900 | 48 | 260 | $0.52 | QA F1 0.75 | quantization drops quality slightly; watch p95 spike
E4 | 2026-02-13 | gpt-large-open | int8 | dynamic batching 32 | enabled | 512 | 5,200 | 80 | 360 | $1.45 | QA F1 0.81 | large model better quality but cost/latency tradeoff
E5 | 2026-02-16 | gpt-medium-open | int8 | adaptive batching (latency-led) | enabled | 256 | 5,800 | 40 | 190 | $0.69 | QA F1 0.78 | adaptive batching keeps tail lower while decent throughput
E6 | 2026-02-18 | gpt-medium-open | int8 + kv-prefetch | dynamic batching 32 | prefetch hints | 256 | 9,100 | 42 | 185 | $0.78 | QA F1 0.79 | KV prefetch helps throughput and lowers p95 in mixed seq runs
E7 | 2026-02-19 | gpt-medium-open | int8 | dynamic batching 32 | enabled | 1024 | 4,200 | 120 | 610 | $0.88 | QA F1 0.76 | long sequences hurt p95 heavily; consider split/streaming

Quick interpretations:
- Best cost reductions seen with 4-bit (E3) but quality drop ~0.03 F1; consider targeted QA-only routing to int8
- KV prefetch (E6) looks promising for typical chat workloads — increases tokens/s and reduces tail compared to baseline
- Adaptive batching (E5) is a nice middle ground for interactive SLOs

Immediate next steps:
- Re-run E3 with prompt-similarity filters to check if quality drop concentrated on long-context QA prompts (owner: me)
- Add simple automated eval harness to run 100 QA prompts across quant settings and output diffs (owner: Jordan) — link: JIRA-987
- Instrument token-level cost logging in canary to validate $/1k estimate (owner: Maya)

To log for retros/notes:
- Ran quick perf runs on dev-dedicated-1; ephemeral noise ~5-8% across runs
- PR draft open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 (profiling + kv prefetch hook)

Scratch TODOs:
- [ ] add column for GPU mem usage per-config
- [ ] add seed column and average across seeds
- [ ] small A/B on routing policy: route high-importance queries to int8-only large model variant

Related links:
- Confluence notes: CONFLUENCE-12345 (llm-inference-mini-experiments)
- Slack thread: #eng-llm-inference (search: kv prefetch results)

Free-form notes / brain dump:
- If we can keep p95 < 220ms for 256/median seq with int8 + kv caching, we should default to that for interactive-tier routes and fallback to 4-bit for batching/cheap async jobs.
- Remember to capture quantization eval per prompt type (code, QA, summarization) — different sensitivity.
- Might be worth a small customer-facing writeup if we get stable numbers (Maya + Product)

Last quick run log (2026-02-20):
- small stability test on dedicated pool (night): 10k tokens generated across mixed prompts; avg cost estimate $0.74/1k; p95 198ms; liveliness OK

End of sheet.
